claims.claim: Roblox was created in 2004 by David Baszucki and Erik Cassel; early in development it was known as DynaBlocks.
claims.notes: Wikipedia, same revision as the Phase 2 brief. Year precision only. The hook's '22 years old' is derived from this date (November 2026 minus 2004 = 22).
Source gives no date for the naming.

claims.claim: Roblox launched to the public on September 1, 2006.
claims.notes: Wikipedia infobox (same revision as claim 1), Release: September 1, 2006.

claims.claim: As of February 2025, Roblox reported an average of 85.3 million daily active users.
claims.notes: Wikipedia (same revision as claim 1). Month precision only. The narration says 'over 85 million players log in daily' — same figure, rounded down. The on-screen source note carries the Feb 2025 date.

claims.claim: Back in 2020, Roblox said over half of all American children under the age of 16 played Roblox. The claim originates in April 2020 (The Verge, from Roblox: 'played by over half of all children in the United States under the age of 16') and was repeated in Roblox's S-1 filing of November 2020.
claims.notes: Month precision only (The Verge, April 2020). The narration dates the claim to 2020 and frames it as what Roblox said — never as a current measurement. The on-screen source note carries the Apr 2020 date.

claims.claim: The Developer Exchange (DevEx) lets creators turn Robux into real money; it launched in 2013 (Robux itself arrived in 2007).
claims.notes: Year precision only for the DevEx launch.

claims.claim: Roblox is 22 years old in November 2026 (created 2004).
claims.notes: Derived number for the hook: 2026 minus 2004 = 22. No new source — arithmetic on claim 1, the verified 2004 creation date.
